overall: Washington DC reached a running max of 86.0°F at 12:45 ET — notably early for a daily high — and temperatures have since dipped to 84.2°F with the 30-minute velocity flatlining at 0.0°F/hr and acceleration turning sharply negative (-1.800°F/hr²). The atmosphere is loaded with moisture (dewpoint ~70°F) and partial cloud cover (62% cloud fraction), with afternoon convection expected by 2pm per NWS, all of which are capping the warming trend well below initial model expectations.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a wide model spread: HRRR is bullish at 92.9°F, ECMWF at 89.9°F, and NBM at 87.8°F — but the current observed running max of only 86.0°F heading into what should be peak heating hours casts doubt on the upper-end NWS call of 93°F. The META model (fused and most reliable) sharply diverges from D1_NOW, concentrating probability in the 86–89°F range (combined ~74%) rather than the 90–91°F bucket that D1_NOW favors at 62.4%.
max_temp_prediction: The balance of evidence points to a daily high in the upper 80s, most likely 87–89°F. The META model's top two even buckets are 86–87°F (39.8%) and 88–89°F (34.2%), and the INTRADAY model echoes this with equal mass in those same buckets. While peak hour models suggest warming could continue until 15–17h ET, the pronounced deceleration, early stall in the running max, and imminent afternoon storm threat (60% PoP) all argue against the HRRR/NWS upper-end scenario. For the active even-bucket Kalshi market, the 90–91°F top bucket appears overpriced relative to what META and intraday dynamics suggest; the 86–87°F and 88–89°F buckets look undervalued.
